clue.text: Vocalist to improvise around unusual chord — it's a must-see

indicators.note: one thing placed around another encloses it, so a piece goes inside the next

parts.note: a vocalist is a singer

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
to scat is to improvise wordless jazz singing

explanation.surface: A singer jams around an odd chord and the show becomes unmissable.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is to read 'Vocalist to improvise' as a possessive pair run together, with the shuffled chord slipped in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In the famous thought experiment, the cat's fate is only settled when someone opens the box and looks, so observation is required.

clue.text: See 1
Slasher presumably showing vamp with a different origin

indicators.note: a different origin means the word's first letter is swapped for another one

parts.note: a vamp is a woman who seduces men

explanation.surface: A horror-film slasher displaying a seductive streak, with an unusual backstory.
explanation.walkthrough: The horror surface makes 'Slasher' a killer; here it is someone slashing prices or costs. SEDUCER loses its first letter S for R.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who slashes prices or budgets cuts them down, which is what a reducer does; 'presumably' flags the whimsical coinage.

clue.text: See 14
Downing Street figure working to upset some players

indicators.note: to upset something is to turn it over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the Prime Minister lives at Number 10 Downing Street
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A government figure in Downing Street sets out to unsettle some team members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a person, but it is the number on the Prime Minister's door: Number 10 Downing Street is the official London residence.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine musicians, so it is a set of players performing together.

clue.text: Wickedness to be sent from below

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending a word upwards from the bottom makes it read backwards

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Evil is something that arrives from the underworld below.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent from below' sounds like a demon from hell, but in a down clue it means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil and wickedness are direct synonyms for moral badness or sinfulness.

clue.text: Part of window showing star now and then — shut it!

indicators.note: now and then means only occasionally, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first and third letters of the word
SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: Someone at a window keeps glimpsing a star and is told to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut it!' is slang for be quiet, the same as the hushing sound SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is the sliding frame holding the glass in a sash window, one component of it.

clue.text: Dom's alibi when travelling is fiendish practice

indicators.note: things that travel move about, so these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Dom's excuse of being away on a trip is a devilish trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored; only the letters of the two words matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolism is devil worship or sorcery, a practice belonging to fiends and demons.

clue.text: Priest cracking hints about contents of early cardinal's tomb

indicators.note: something cracking breaks apart, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: PR is a standard abbreviation for priest
hints are clues
HE, His Eminence, is the formal style of a cardinal

explanation.surface: A priest breaks into an old cardinal's tomb, prompted by clues about what lies inside.
explanation.walkthrough: A cardinal is addressed as His Eminence, abbreviated HE. The parse is uncertain: these pieces supply every letter, but how 'about contents of early' fits the setter's design is unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepulchre is a burial chamber or vault cut in rock or built of stone, the same thing as a tomb.

clue.text: Methuselah had to complete a course his boss thought up

parts.note: Methuselah is the setter, so 'Methuselah had' is I'D
you finish a course of a meal by eating it
the setter's boss is the editor, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: The setter had to finish a course of study that his manager devised.
explanation.walkthrough: Methuselah is the setter's pseudonym, so his name stands for I or ME; a setter's boss is the crossword editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To ideate is to form an idea or concept, so something ideated has been conceived or invented in the mind.

clue.text: Naked man possibly relieves 28 older women

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters are taken off

parts.note: the word with its outside letters stripped
to untie is to free or relieve, here acting on the troublemaker at 28

explanation.surface: A nude man comes to the rescue of some elderly ladies plagued by a mischievous creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is uncertain: A plus UNTIES gives the letters, but the role of 'possibly' and the cross-reference to 28 is unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunties is an affectionate term for older women generally, not only relatives, as in agony aunt.

clue.text: With lead characters lost, hob must cast spells

indicators.note: losing the lead characters means the opening letter of each word is dropped
to cast metal is to remould it, so these letters are formed into a new order

parts.note: both words without their first letters

explanation.surface: A goblin, minus its leaders, has to cast magic spells.
explanation.walkthrough: A hob is a hobgoblin, which supports the witchcraft reading of 'cast spells'; the definition is spells as in periods of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout is a short period of activity or illness, just as a spell is, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Letters regularly dispatched from US to African capital

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at fixed intervals, so every second letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Mail is regularly sent from America to an African capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African capital' looks like the definition but the city is in Bulgaria, not Africa; 'African' just supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria, the seat of its government.

clue.text: Stirring cauldron, cut a sinister figure

indicators.note: stirring mixes contents around, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A witch stirring her cauldron looks a menacing figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like the verb of the surface (to cut a figure) but its letters belong to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker's vampire is one of fiction's most menacing villains, an archetypal creature of horror.

clue.text: Little attention seekers in hotel with things available at reception

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
with and 'and' both join things together
a hotel front desk has a bell to ring for service

explanation.surface: Small needy guests in a hotel, alongside the amenities offered at the front desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little attention seekers' suggests attention-hungry children; it is small bells rung to call someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbell is a small bell rung by hand, used to summon servants or get people's notice.

clue.text: Initiating another session about action on pitch

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
booting the ball is kicking it on a football pitch

explanation.surface: Starting a fresh meeting to discuss what happened on the playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a surface preposition but is the piece RE; 'pitch' is a sports field, not a sales pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebooting a computer restarts it and begins a new working session, hence a fresh start.

clue.text: One sent down for good over unsuccessful coup, originally

definitions.text: One sent down for good over unsuccessful coup, originally

parts.words: One sent down for good over unsuccessful coup
parts.note: surface: a prisoner jailed for life after a failed attempt to seize power
setter's reading: at the very beginning, the angel cast out of heaven forever after rebelling against God

explanation.surface: A failed rebel is imprisoned for life after a botched takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent down' is British for jailed, and 'for good' means permanently; both also fit being cast out of heaven, and 'originally' points to the first rebellion of all.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian tradition the rebel angel was thrown from heaven for leading a revolt against God, becoming Satan.

clue.text: Endangered bat's taken to have wings clipped

indicators.note: clipping a bird's wings trims its edges, so the outer letters are cut off

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored; the letters run on unbroken, so trimming them is the whole trick, not a coincidence

explanation.surface: A threatened bat species has been captured and had its wings trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The bat is not the definition; 'Endangered' is, and the bat's letters lose their first and last.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at stake is at risk of being lost, so it is in peril or under threat.

clue.text: Sharp, stinging pain

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a sharp burning hurt

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it describes a single pain; split after 'Sharp', it gives an adjective and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means clever or keen, and as a noun it is the sting felt from a slap or wound.

clue.text: A-list brought on board to create comedies

indicators.note: being on board means inside a ship, so one piece sits inside the steamship letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the conventional 'board' of a ship
the A-list is the cream, the best of the best

explanation.surface: Celebrities are signed up to make funny films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is the ship convention: words go inside SS. In a Halloween puzzle the answer also suggests horror rather than comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hilarious is informally called a scream, so screams are very funny things such as comedies.

clue.text: Sign of cross almost knocked European character over

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
something knocked about is jolted out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word without its final letter
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a European script
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: The sign of the cross, nearly knocked over by someone from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign of cross' looks like making the sign of the cross; the definition is only 'Sign', a zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio, the scorpion, is the eighth of the twelve astrological star signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Old devil's got a couple of old stars forgetting their lines

indicators.note: L is the abbreviation for line, and forgetting it means leaving that letter out

parts.note: Sol is the old Roman name for the sun, our star; the clue wants two of them
a couple is two things put together, joined by 'and'

explanation.surface: A rascal has two veteran actors who keep drying up on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars forgetting their lines' sounds like actors drying; it is two SOLs each losing L, linked by AND. The parse is uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild euphemism for a scoundrel or rascal, as in 'you old so-and-so'.

clue.text: A portion of scrambled egg on salmon's picked up and necked

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking something up lifts it, so it reads from bottom to top
a portion is only part of the whole, so the letters lie inside the phrase

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word to the start of the last

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into scrambled egg on smoked salmon, then picks it up and gulps it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrambled' is not an anagram signal here; it is part of the phrase concealing the letters. Snogging is British slang for kissing passionately.
explanation.definitionFit: To neck is informal for kissing and cuddling, as is the British slang verb used here.

clue.text: Tolkien has him following a ring of gold around

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the letter O is ring-shaped
French d'or means of gold, as in the Ballon d'Or

explanation.surface: Tolkien writes of a character trailing after a golden ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The one ring of the surface is apt, since Frodo carries it. The definition is the whole phrase 'Tolkien has him', a hobbit in The Lord of the Rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Frodo Baggins is the hobbit hero of The Lord of the Rings, created by Tolkien.

clue.text: Gothic building in which there's a lack of reflection

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an ornamental structure, often a mock ruin, built for show
second meaning: foolishness, acting without thinking

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lack of reflection' hints at a vampire with no mirror image in a Gothic house; here reflection means careful thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Landowners built decorative mock-Gothic towers called follies, and the same word means foolishness or thoughtless behaviour.

clue.text: Part of a Halloween tradition where a sucker is made to welcome a little rascal

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a teat is what a baby sucks
the first letter of rascal, a little of it

explanation.surface: At Halloween a gullible person ends up hosting a mischievous child at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' looks like a dupe but is the teat on a bottle; 'little rascal' looks like a trick-or-treating child but supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Trick or treat is the custom of children demanding sweets at Halloween; the second half is the reward.

clue.text: Sorceress wants women to tickle

indicators.note: to want is to lack, so a letter is missing

parts.note: a witch is a sorceress
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A sorceress desires women to tickle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wants' reads as desires, but here means lacks, as in found wanting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tickle and an itch are both irritating sensations on the skin that make you want to scratch.

clue.text: Dress like a folk-tale wolf we've heard about

indicators.note: something heard rather than read is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a werewolf is a man who turns into a wolf in folklore

explanation.surface: Clothes that make you look like the wolf in a fairy tale, as rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Red Riding Hood's wolf in grandma's clothes; the piece is the prefix of werewolf.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear clothes is to dress in them, and as nouns both mean clothing, as in evening wear.

clue.text: Fancy gadget shown in Bond film's teaser?

parts.note: a tie is a bond
a clip is a short extract used to tease a film

explanation.surface: A spy gadget glimpsed in the trailer for a James Bond film.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond seems to be 007, whose films are full of gadgets; it is just a tie, and the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie clip is an ornamental accessory clamping a necktie to the shirt, a decorative little device.

clue.text: Troublemaker finally blowing entrance off Vlad's castle

indicators.note: with the entrance taken off, the opening letter is removed
finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
Vladimir Putin's seat of power is the Kremlin, a Moscow fortress

explanation.surface: A vandal blows the gate off Dracula's castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Vlad suggests Vlad the Impaler and Dracula's castle in this Halloween puzzle; it is Vladimir Putin, and the castle is the Kremlin.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary mischievous creature blamed for mechanical faults, so it causes trouble.

clue.text: Ultimately obsolete little contraction which we still use occasionally today

definitions.text: Ultimately obsolete little contraction which we still use occasionally today

parts.note: surface: an outdated abbreviated word, a poetic shortening of evening

parts.words: which we still use occasionally today
parts.note: setter's reading: the shortening survives once a year, at the end of the October festival named in this puzzle's theme

explanation.walkthrough: The archaic shortening of evening lives on in Hallowe'en, used on one occasion each year: today, the puzzle's publication date being Halloween.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the poetic shortened form of evening, archaic now except in the name of the All Hallows festival.

clue.text: Pole gives attack dog the slip and joins two Italians who escaped long ago

indicators.note: giving someone the slip means escaping them, so a letter leaves its word

parts.note: to harry is to harass or attack
a hound is a dog

indicators.note: to join a pair is to come between them, so a piece is placed in the middle

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for Italian, twice
N, the North Pole

explanation.surface: A Polish man evades a guard dog and teams up with two Italians in an old escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is N; the letter that leaves the dog reappears between the two Italians.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Houdini was a famous escapologist of the early twentieth century, celebrated for slipping out of chains and locked tanks.
